morph.note: Perfect third plural of √वृष् (reduplication व-वर्ष्-). ‘To rain’ takes the target in the accusative: तां देवीं ववर्षुः ‘they rained upon the Goddess’.
Nominative plural of the i-stem अरि with guṇa: -अयः.

mantras.anvaya: ततः उद्धतामर्षाः अमरारयः प्रथमम् एव अग्रे तां देवीं शरशक्त्यृष्टिवृष्टिभिः ववर्षुः।
mantras.anvaya_en: Subject (अमरारयः) with its qualifier, adverbs of time and place, object, instrument, verb.
mantras.lit: Then at the very first, in front, the enemies of the immortals, their indignation roused, rained upon that Goddess with showers of arrows, spears and swords.
mantras.tr: Then the enemies of the gods, their fury roused, at once rained down on the Goddess from the front showers of arrows, spears and swords.

comm.t: The asuras strike first, answering the message with a volley of missiles. ऋष्टि is a sword or two-edged blade; शक्ति here is the hurled spear.
The image of weapons as rain recurs in the next chapter, where Śumbha and Niśumbha pour arrows on the Goddess ‘like two clouds raining’ (9.9: मेघयोरिव वर्षतोः).

samasa.vigraha: शूलाः च शक्तयः च परश्वधाः च, तान्
आध्मातं धनुः आध्मातधनुः (karmadhāraya); आध्मातधनुषः मुक्ताः, तैः
महान्तः च ते इषवः च, तैः

morph.note: Perfect of √छिद्: the reduplicated syllable has c for ch (चि-), and ch after a short vowel is doubled to cch (चिच्छेद).
आध्मात is the past participle of आ + √ध्मा ‘to blow’: the bow is ‘blown’, i.e. made to resound as it is drawn and loosed.
Past participle of प्र + √हि ‘to send forth’: the weapons the asuras had hurled (8.30).
An itaretara dvandva takes the gender of its last member: परश्वध is masculine, so the accusative plural is -आन्, agreeing with तान् प्रहितान्.

mantras.anvaya: सा च आध्मातधनुर्मुक्तैः महेषुभिः तान् प्रहितान् बाणान् शूलशक्तिपरश्वधान् (च) लीलया चिच्छेद।
mantras.anvaya_en: Subject, instrument (महेषुभिः with its qualifier), two objects qualified by तान् प्रहितान्, adverb of manner, verb.
mantras.lit: And she, with great arrows loosed from her resounding bow, cut with ease those launched arrows, pikes, spears and axes.
mantras.tr: And with great arrows loosed from her thrumming bow she cut down, as if in play, the arrows, pikes, spears and axes they had hurled.

comm.t: The Goddess cuts every missile in the air. The word लीलया, ‘in play’, is the narrator’s mark of her ease.

The same word marks her battles in every carita: she cuts the weapons ‘as if in play’ at 2.50 and 3.4, and breaks Śumbha’s weapons so at 10.13 (लीलयैव). The tradition reads the divine acts of creation and destruction as her play (līlā).
The Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) gives the idea a cosmic scale: name 648, लीलाकॢप्तब्रह्माण्डमण्डला, ‘who fashioned the sphere of the universe in play’.

samasa.literal: torn apart by the falls of the spear

morph.note: Feminine present participle of √कृ (stem कुर्वत्), with a double accusative: अरीन् (object) and the two participles (what she made them) — ‘making the enemies torn and crushed’.
Imperfect with the augment between prefix and root: वि + अ + चरत्. Contrast the augmentless उपबृंहयत् of 8.9.
पोथित is the past participle of the causative of √पुथ् ‘to crush’ (पोथयति). The khaṭvāṅga, a staff topped with a skull, is Kālī’s weapon from her first appearance (7.7, 7.15).

mantras.anvaya: तदा काली तथा तस्य अग्रतः अरीन् शूलपातविदारितान् खट्वाङ्गपोथितान् च कुर्वती व्यचरत्।
mantras.anvaya_en: Subject (काली) with the participle phrase कुर्वती (object अरीन्, two predicate accusatives); place (तस्य अग्रतः); verb व्यचरत्.
mantras.lit: Likewise Kālī then ranged in front of it, making the enemies torn by the blows of her spear and crushed by her khaṭvāṅga.
mantras.tr: So too Kālī ranged at the front of the fight, tearing the foe with blows of her spear and crushing them with her skull-staff.
mantras.tr_note: तस्य अग्रतः, ‘in front of it/him’, is rendered ‘at the front of the fight’; see the flag.

comm.t: Kālī fights in the van with spear and khaṭvāṅga. The Mothers’ deeds follow one by one (8.33–38).
The khaṭvāṅga was Kālī’s weapon from her first appearance (7.7: विचित्रखट्वाङ्गधरा), and the asuras fell to it then as now (7.15: खट्वाङ्गताडिताः).

flags.uncertain: तस्य is masculine or neuter: most naturally the enemy host (सैन्यम्), at whose front Kālī ranges, or Śiva, last named in 8.29. Many renderings take it as ‘before her (Caṇḍikā)’, which would need तस्याः; that reading treats the masculine as a licence.
